question: Can extra training improve the final tree by transferring how two different teachers handle ambiguity, even if mixing their final answers gives little lift? Test cross-fitted soft targets on the training side.
training: Within 4061 fitting rows, divide identical full-feature rows together into four stratified folds with seed 72731. Fit a recurring-context tree and a verified TabICLv2 classifier on the other three folds for each row. Every training row gets predictions from two teachers that did not see it or its identical-feature group. Keep every original outcome as the majority of its student target. One student mixes 30 percent mean teacher probability; the second uses up to 45 percent scaled by teacher agreement and confidence. Use a single recurring-context tree per student trained with CrossEntropy and the original hard-label feature selection. Eight shared teacher fits and two student fits. Do not learn a new teacher policy after seeing confirmations.
assessment: Save all predictions before the 808-row nomination. Compare each student standalone or with shares .125, .25 or .5 of the fixed research pair, permit retention, confirm on the separate 817 and 807 training rows. No fall in either plus pooled +.003 is required to proceed to ordinary-entry comparisons. No designated validation, final test, new task data or model API.
